candidates.title: Congruences modulo powers of $2$ and $3$ for Lin's function $\text{PDO}_t(n)$
candidates.comment: 19 pages; Page 18 contains a detailed AI Disclosure statement; comments are welcome
candidates.abstract: Let $\text{PDO}_t(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Confirming a conjecture of Singh and Barman (2025), Tang (2026) recently proved that $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{2m-1}n)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+1}}$ for all $m\geq1$ and $n\geq0$. Using elementary techniques, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{m+2}n)$, and we use them to determine $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ modulo one further power of $2$. More precisely, we show that the quotient of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ by the relevant power of $2$ is odd exactly when $n$ is an odd square, or $2$, $3$ or $6$ times an odd square, depending on $k$. As a consequence, we obtain several new infinite families of congruences modulo arbitrary powers of $2$, such as \[ \text{PDO}_t\bigl(3\times4^{m}(3n+2)\bigr)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+4}}, \] and \[\text{PDO}_t\bigl(3\times4^{m}(6n+5)\bigr)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+5}}. \] We also obtain an analogous improvement of a result of Li and Tang (2026) modulo powers of $3$, and an infinite family of internal congruences modulo powers of $2$.

candidates.title: Censored Regression Models with Endogeneity: A Survey
candidates.abstract: This survey article provides a comprehensive overview of methodologies developed to handle endogeneity in censored regression models. We emphasize their theoretical basis, and estimating methodologies. The paper summarizes the benefits and drawbacks of each technique and addresses expansions to nonlinear, panel, and high-dimensional settings, offering researchers practical assistance and identifying options for future methodological improvement in censored models with endogenous regressors.

candidates.title: Perturbed QMC designs and reduced QMC strength
candidates.abstract: Small errors in sampling locations can change the convergence rate of a cubature rule. We study this effect for equal-weight integration on spheres and determine how accurately the nodes must be realized to retain optimal Sobolev rates. Under an average energy condition on the reference nodes, we establish sharp perturbation bounds and characterize how the decay of node errors affects quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) strength, which measures the smoothness range over which optimal rates hold. We identify when this strength is preserved and when it can decrease, and show that sufficiently slow decay of node errors can destroy all optimal Sobolev rates. For a reference rule with optimal convergence, we further establish a necessary and sufficient condition on node accuracy for retaining the optimal rate uniformly over all permitted perturbations. Numerical experiments with spherical designs, Fekete points, and Coulomb-energy points illustrate the different stability regimes.

candidates.title: Orthosymplectic $K$-matrices in small dimensions
candidates.abstract: Using elementary methods, we describe coideal subalgebras of quantum orthosymplectic algebras of small dimensions, classify the corresponding $K$-matrices and find explicitly the centralizers of these subalgebras in the vector representation. The main attention is paid to generators with a Cartan term. For them, at generic values of the parameters, we find the centralizers and all $K$-matrices and describe the decomposition of the vector representation over the coideal subalgebra. We find all special values of the parameters of two types and, at a generic point of each set of special values, describe the decomposition of the vector representation and all $K$-matrices. At special values of the first type the dimension of the centralizer grows. One hypersurface of such values is related to Cartan terms, and on it one of the generators is given by the same formula as in the quantum electrical algebra. At special values of the second type the dimension of the centralizer is the same, but nonzero nilpotent elements appear in it. The $K$-matrices on the sets of special values of the second type are obtained from those already found by substituting the condition, and there are no others.

candidates.title: An Algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay
candidates.abstract: A 4-dimensional algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay over an arbitrary field is constructed. Furthermore, it is shown that every three-dimensional graded ASL domain is Cohen--Macaulay.

candidates.title: Differentiability of the solution to an SPDE with respect to the model for the associated regularity structure
candidates.abstract: Given a stochastic partial differential equation that falls within the scope of the theory of regularity structures, we show that its solution is, in a suitable sense, a smooth function of the underlying model. This allows one to infer the regularity of the solution with respect to any perturbation of the noise from that of the model. As an application of our results, we provide an elementary proof of the Malliavin differentiability of solutions to a wide class of equations driven by Gaussian noises.

candidates.title: Coordinate Ordering and Non-collinear Central Configurations
candidates.abstract: We establish a mass-independent criterion for N-body central configurations based on a special coordinate ordering of the bodies. Moreover, we identify a region in the plane that contains no non-collinear central configurations. This provides a way to exclude non-collinear central configurations that are nearly collinear.

candidates.title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
candidates.abstract: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.

candidates.title: Tuning the false discovery rate in the closed eBH procedure
candidates.abstract: The closed eBH procedure controls the false discovery rate under arbitrary dependence between the input e-values. It takes the target false discovery rate $α$ as its input and outputs a rejection set $R$, the usual goal being to maximize its size $\left|R\right|$. This note discusses a modification of the closed eBH procedure that allows choosing the target false discovery rate post hoc: the rejection set and its level $α$ can be chosen after seeing the data, and the expected ratio of the false discovery proportion to $α$ is at most 1. We adapt Vovk and Wang's (2023) algorithm for computing discovery e-matrices to computing, in quadratic time, the frontier of achievable combinations $(\left|R\right|,α)$ of the size of a rejection set $R$ and its level $α$. The frontier allows us to compute an optimal rejection set in view of a given utility function $F$, $F(\left|R\right|,α)\to\max$, striking a balance between the goals of reducing $α$ and increasing $\left|R\right|$.

candidates.title: Exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions
candidates.abstract: We study exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions whose conditional mean consists of a linear term and a signed adapted perturbation. The linear term determines a product normalization, but convergence after normalization does not ensure a strictly positive limit. Multiplying the state by the inverse of each deterministic contraction factor gives a contraction-adjusted state. On paths where this state tends to infinity, we prove that the logarithm of the normalized state differs from the cumulative relative perturbation by an almost surely convergent quantity. The assumptions control the effective step sizes, the quadratic positive relative perturbation, and the conditional quadratic variation of the relative martingale noise. If the positive perturbation is summable at the normalized scale, the normalized process converges to a finite non-negative limit; strict positivity is then equivalent to absolute summability of the relative perturbation. We also give criteria for divergence of the contraction-adjusted state, first-order comparisons, and counterexamples illustrating the role of the hypotheses. candidates.title: The Space of $k$-Positive Potentials
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we study weak geodesics in the space of $k$-positive potentials on a compact Kähler manifold. We prove that any two smooth strictly $k$-positive potentials can be joined by a weak geodesic of class $C^{1,1}$. As an application, we prove that the pair $(\mathcal H_k,d_2)$ is a metric space.

candidates.title: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III

candidates.abstract: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$. As a consequence, every such family admits strong $\varepsilon$-nets of size at most $5000h/\varepsilon$.

candidates.title: Finsler--Sobolev inequalities: optimality & rigidity
candidates.abstract: We establish optimal Sobolev and logarithmic-Sobolev inequalities on non-compact, possibly non-reversible Finsler manifolds with non-negative weighted Ricci curvature. The optimal constants exhibit no dependence on reversibility -- confirming Ohta's conjectural principle -- being governed solely by the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios. We then apply the logarithmic-Sobolev inequality to establish the optimal hypercontractivity estimate for the heat flow in the same geometric setting. The equality cases of the above optimal inequalities imply strong rigidity in the underlying manifold, characterized by fine properties of the flag and $S$-curvatures as well as the precise profiles of the corresponding extremizers. We illustrate our results by examples including Randers metrics obtained by Zermelo navigation with Killing vector fields, and weighted convex cones in $\mathbb{R}^n$ endowed with arbitrary Minkowski norms, the latter showing that the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios may differ.

candidates.title: KAM theory for contact Hamiltonian systems
candidates.abstract: In both finite and infinite dimensions, we establish the first frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian families with general analytic coupling between the momenta and the contact variable. After adjustment of external parameters, the flow on each torus is analytically conjugate in the original time to the prescribed translation, with estimates uniform as the damping parameter crosses zero. This coupling can generate nonzero mean damping at first order even when the damping parameter vanishes. In finite dimensions, nonzero mean damping yields a time-preserving analytic contact linearization near the torus. In both settings the invariant graphs give global analytic solutions of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations whose characteristic flows are conjugate to the prescribed translation. A novel consequence in finite dimensions is that, under global Tonelli assumptions and strict increase in the contact variable, this analytic solution is both the unique forward and the unique backward weak KAM solution, and its associated Legendrian graph is an invariant torus carrying quasi-periodic dynamics.

candidates.title: Some attractive bases for the Onsager Lie algebra
candidates.abstract: The Onsager Lie algebra $\mathcal{O}$ is defined by generators $A$, $B$ subject to the Dolan-Grady relations $[A,[A,[A,B]]] = 4[A,B]$ and $[B,[B,[B,A]]] = 4[B,A]$. It is known that $\mathcal{O}$ is infinite-dimensional. In this paper, we consider three bases for $\mathcal{O}$. The first basis was recently introduced by the author, and the second basis is a variation of the first. The third basis was introduced by Baseilhac and Crampé in 2019. By construction, the elements in each basis are recursively obtained from $A$, $B$. Using the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ loop algebra, we express every basis element in closed form. We then describe how these three bases are related to each other. Next, we consider a finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-module $V$. Associated with $V$ are six well-known decompositions: the eigenspace decomposition of $A$ and the eigenspace decomposition of $B$, together with four other decompositions of $V$ said to be split. We show that on each decomposition, every element of the first two bases acts in a block diagonal, block upper bidiagonal, block lower bidiagonal, or block tridiagonal fashion. candidates.title: The Schürmann-Vallentin lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering in dimension six
candidates.comment: 37 pages, accompanying computational package available at https://github.com/alexeygarber/6dim-lattice-covering
candidates.abstract: We prove that the lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ discovered by Schürmann and Vallentin in 2006 is the unique (up to similarity) six-dimensional lattice that gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering.

candidates.title: Data-driven discovery of sparse governing equations with parameterized operators
candidates.abstract: We study parameterized SINDy (pSINDy), an extension of the Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) framework for the discovery of parsimonious governing equations involving operators with unknown parameters such as fractional-order Caputo derivatives, fractional Laplacians, and parameterized kernel operators. The framework jointly identifies the unknown operator parameters and sparse library coefficients through a sparsity-promoting optimization problem. To solve this problem, we develop and analyze the parameterized sequentially thresholded least-squares (pSTLSQ) algorithm. In each iteration, it removes terms with small coefficients, updates the operator parameters by a fixed number of optimization steps that improve the fit of the remaining library terms, and refits their coefficients by least squares. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that pSTLSQ converges locally to a local minimizer and give sufficient conditions for identifying the terms present in the governing equation. Numerical experiments demonstrate recovery of governing equations from noisy synthetic data for fractional ODEs, fractional PDEs, and nonlocal diffusion equations. We also examine the influenc

candidates.title: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
candidates.abstract: Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[ |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$. The proof's key idea is to run the prime-field Stepanov method in reverse, constructing an auxiliary polynomial whose specialization vanishes identically instead of requiring it to be nonzero.

candidates.title: Mechanism Design under Belief Disagreement: Allocation Flexibility and Rent Capacity
candidates.abstract: A seller jointly chooses allocation and payments when buyers misperceive competition. Under independent private values, statewise participation, and payment restrictions, allocation determines both required rents and their delivery capacity. We separate these effects under a common subjective law. For three values and shared-top beliefs, explicit score and capacity conditions characterize globally optimal lower-value lotteries, including top-rent overflow and welfare differences among revenue optima. A two-buyer construction establishes a strict allocation advantage over every reserve under the same fixed reporting certificate and positive margin. A transport test and exact band-boundary incentive equalities identify separate conditions restoring objective-law revenue ceilings. For three bands and a common affine belief interval, an explicitly certified reserve attains the ceiling under stated score conditions. A case scaled to public collectible-auction records yields a nominal shared-top allocation gain of 24.72 cents per auction. A one-cent report-by-report margin yields matched gains of 1.48 cents under projection and 3.32 cents under shared-top beliefs; the three-band point-be

candidates.title: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation
candidates.abstract: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry. By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlinear moment as an equivalence class of functions rather than a function. The polynomial of degree $N$ or formal power series ansatz of the invariance equation are the distinguished representatives of the equivalence class. We also show that, when the system is exponentially stable, the moment describ

candidates.title: Sharp $s$-nice recurrence without the van der Corput property
candidates.abstract: For every real $s>2$, we construct a set $R_s\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ which is a set of $t$-nice measurable recurrence exactly for $t\ge s$ and is not a van der Corput set. The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--Rödl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure $σ_s$ which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass $(s-2)/(2s-2)$. A Gaussian tail argument proves both sharpness of the recurrence exponent and the fact that this atom is the largest possible for any $s$-nice recurrent set. The result sharpens the recurrence separations of Bourgain and Mountakis, answers a question of Mountakis about the maximal mass of an atom at zero, and answers a question of Forrest about separating the various degrees of nice recurrence. In the appendix we give a self-contained proof of the Density Frankl-Rödl theorem.

candidates.title: Kleinian groups generated by two elliptics of even order
candidates.abstract: Let $Γ<\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ be a non-elementary discrete group generated by two elliptics of even order, with a nontrivial relation in the corresponding free product of cyclic groups. We classify the possible compact orbifold cores of $\mathbb H^3/Γ$, together with their cusp data and marked meridians. They are finite meridional fillings of the two-bridge link and Heckoid models of Akiyoshi--Ohshika--Parker--Sakuma--Yoshida. Their weighted graphs have at most two standard tunnels, whose weights in the two-tunnel case are $2$ and an odd integer. The original generators are powers of primitive meridians which generate $Γ$, and we determine the possible meridian placements for all even orders. The groups are geometrically finite, their conformal boundary components are turnovers, and each oriented core with its cusp data determines its complete hyperbolic holonomy up to Möbius conjugacy. The proof uses trace rigidity, dihedral surgery, half-turn symmetries, and an index-two cover.

candidates.title: An Elasticity Complex for Kirchhoff--Love Shells
candidates.abstract: We develop an elasticity complex for Kirchhoff--Love shell theory, based on the linearized Gauss--Codazzi equations as compatibility conditions for shell strains. The resulting shell complex forms a fine resolution of the sheaf of infinitesimal rigid motions, so its cohomology groups are determined by the corresponding sheaf cohomology. Remarkably, the complex also reveals an Airy potential representation of equilibrium stress fields. The framework further identifies natural boundary conditions for both kinematic and dynamic variables. Finally, we establish a Hodge--Morrey--Friedrichs decomposition for strain and stress fields on shells with boundary.

candidates.title: On the tensor product of semistable Hermitian adelic vector bundles over an adelic curve
candidates.abstract: We prove tensor semistability for Hermitian adelic vector bundles on proper adelic curves whose underlying fields are countable and of characteristic zero. The central estimate concerns the canonical integral Specht lattice of a rectangular partition with fixed height: its logarithmic covolume, divided by its rank and tensor degree, tends to zero. We prove this estimate from monic seminormal norms and an exact hypergeometric law weighted by the square of a Vandermonde product for tableau prefixes. Constant adelic Specht bundles and equivariant contractions then yield the slope inequality for every geometrically semistable subspace of a finite tensor product. The correction is the measure of the Archimedean places times a sublinear Specht term and vanishes in the limit as the auxiliary degree tends to infinity. An instability-filtration argument completes the reduction to arbitrary factors and identifies the tensor product Harder--Narasimhan filtration. The number field specialization gives the Bost tensor semistability conjecture in all ranks.

candidates.title: Lattices of Minimal Covolume in $\mathrm{SL}_2$ over Dyadic Local Fields
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we determine the minimal covolume among lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ for each finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_2$. Using the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ on its Bruhat--Tits tree, we investigate the shape of the fixed subtrees of finite subgroups, particularly cyclic and dicyclic subgroups of $2$-power order. We determine which larger vertex stabilizers can occur at boundary vertices of the fixed subtrees of dicyclic subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $2.A_4$. We use these results to construct graphs of groups defining lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ and prove that these lattices attain the minimal covolume. This extends a result of Lubotzky and Weigel, which treats finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for odd primes $p$.

candidates.title: On p-Group Actions and Index Divisibilities
candidates.abstract: We prove a mod-$ p $ divisibility result for indices of elliptic operators assuming a smooth action by a finite $ p $-group on the base manifold of dimension $ n\le 2(p-1) $ with no stationary points and which lifts equivariantly to the operator bundles. We show as one consequence that if such manifolds are spin or stably almost complex, with the group action lifting to the relevant structure, then their class in the relevant bordism theory modulo $ p $ is fully determined by one genus, and indeed vanishes for $ n<2(p-1) $. We show as another consequence that there exists no closed connected $ 24 $-dimensional spin manifold $ M $ satisfying $ {\hat{A}(M)=1}, {\hat{A}(M;T_\mathbb{C}M)=0} $, and for which there exists a smooth non-trivial action by the monster group, resolving a question of Hirzebruch.

candidates.title: Sub-Riemannian flow matching
candidates.abstract: We study sub-Riemannian conditional flow matching (SRCFM) for generative transport with prescribed velocity constraints. Training uses paths between sampled source and target points whose velocities lie in the allowed horizontal directions at each state. A neural network takes time and the full state as input and predicts the coefficients of these directions, and the horizontal frame then determines the full velocity used for generation. We describe constructions based on Heisenberg geodesics and joint endpoint equations in free step-two Carnot groups. We propose a scalable piecewise algorithm that computes horizontal paths directly from their endpoints. A straight segment sets the horizontal coordinates, and a loop in those coordinates corrects the remaining vertical displacement. We verify the algorithm's endpoint accuracy to numerical precision in high-dimensional tests. Synthetic experiments illustrate approximate distribution transport along horizontal trajectories. On resized MNIST, we use the same construction to generate images from Gaussian inputs with fewer controls than pixels.

candidates.title: Similarity preserving noncommutative maps
candidates.abstract: In this note we study similarity preserving automorphisms of noncommutative (NC for short) balls. We show that every similarity preserving NC automorphism is, in fact, given by a similarity with an NC invertible function. As an application, we show that the group of automorphisms of the free semigroup algebra is generated by unitarily implemented and inner automorphisms.

candidates.title: Computing pro-$p$ Closures of Finitely Generated Subgroups of Closed Orientable Surface Groups
candidates.abstract: Let $Γ_g$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g\geq2$, and let $p$ be a prime. For every finitely generated subgroup $H\leqΓ_g$ we give an algorithm which, given any finite generating set of $H$ by words in a standard generating set, outputs a finite set of words in the same alphabet that generates the pro-$p$ closure of $H$. This extends the computation of pro-$p$ closures in free groups by Ribes-Zalesskii and Margolis-Sapir-Weil.

candidates.title: Improved bounds for the binary Chowla conjecture
candidates.abstract: For the Möbius function $μ$ and every fixed $0 < ε< 1$, we prove \[ \sum_{n \le x} μ(n) μ(n + 1) \ll_ε \frac{x}{(\log x)^{1 - ε}}. \] This improves on OpenAI's recent bound of $x/(\log x)^c$, where $c > 0$ is a tiny absolute constant. The proof echoes the graph expansion framework of Helfgott, Radziwill, and Pilatte on the logarithmic Chowla conjecture, earlier Fourier analytic methods of Matomäki, Radziwill, and Tao on the Chowla conjecture on average, as well as work of Teräväinen and the author for Möbius on shifted primes. This also yields an improved result, \[ \sum_{p \le x} μ(p + 2) \ll_ε \frac{π(x)}{(\log x)^{1/2 - ε}}. \] Specifically, we refine the determinant approach from the Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors. We replace the averaged prime weights of Lü-Wang-Wu with an exact partition of prime intervals. Once sieving out exceptional integers, this enables uniform cancellation with arbitrary log power savings.

candidates.title: Louis Bachelier's Theorie de la speculation: Circulation and Reception
candidates.abstract: Louis Bachelier's Theorie de la speculation (1900) introduced a probabilistic model of Brownian motion in a study of financial fluctuations, five years before Einstein's physical theory. By connecting probability distributions with the heat equation and studying speculation and option valuation, Bachelier anticipated central developments in probability, physics, and mathematical finance. How widely did the thesis circulate before its broader significance was recognized? Drawing on library correspondence, surviving copies, accession registers, provenance marks, historical catalogues, and acquisition lists, this article reconstructs its international circulation and reception in two forms: the separate Gauthier-Villars dissertation and its publication in the Annales scientifiques de l'Ecole normale superieure. It identifies thirty-eight foreign academic institutions in the official dissertation exchange network for 1900 and documents its operation. University exchanges, commercial purchases, journal distribution, and personal presentations provided complementary channels. American holdings reveal its geographical reach, including receipt at Cornell in April 1900. Contemporary reviews

candidates.title: Topology-Preserving Hodge--Laplacian Diffusion on Manifolds with Boundary
candidates.abstract: Overview: We study deterministic and stochastic Hodge--Laplacian diffusion of differential forms on a fixed smooth compact Riemannian manifold with boundary. Absolute and relative boundary conditions select harmonic spaces representing ordinary and relative cohomology. We investigate the preservation properties of these diffusion processes, their compatible cellular discretizations, and their implications for reverse diffusion models. Numerical experiments on an annulus and a solid torus illustrate the theoretical results. Mathematical Significance: Using the de Rham complex and its constant-sheaf interpretation, we distinguish preservation of harmonic coordinates from preservation of a cohomology class. We establish that deterministic heat flow preserves the harmonic projection and exponentially damps its orthogonal complement. For additive stochastic forcing, we prove that pathwise harmonic preservation is equivalent to the absence of harmonic noise. Exact forcing preserves closedness and the initial cohomology class for closed initial data, whereas harmonic-projected forcing need not preserve closedness. candidates.title: Computability of states and non-computability of traces
candidates.abstract: We study computable presentations of the state space and trace space of computably presented C*-algebras. We show that the state space has a computably compact presentation with respect to which the evaluation of states is a computable map. As an application of having computable states, we obtain a computable version of the GNS construction. We show that the trace space does not share these computational properties. Specifically, we give an example of a computable presentation of a simple AF algebra for which the trace space has no computably compact presentation with respect to which evaluation is computable. As a consequence, we demonstrate that the Elliott invariant of a computably presentable classifiable C*-algebra is not always presentable in a way that makes all key features of the invariant computable.

candidates.title: Sharp Estimates for Jacobi Heat Kernels on a Ball and on a Simplex in the Full Range of Parameters
candidates.abstract: We establish genuinely sharp heat-kernel estimates for orthogonal expansions on the Euclidean unit ball and on the unit simplex throughout their natural parameter ranges. For the ball weight $W_μ(x)=(1-\|x\|^2)^{μ-1/2}$, we extend the known estimate from the range $μ\geq0$ to every $μ>-1/2$. For the simplex, we prove the corresponding estimate for every $κ\in(-1/2,\infty)^{d+1}$. The estimates retain exactly the form known in the classical ranges. The proof is based on analytic continuation of the classical product and reduction formulas. Below the integrability threshold, the ball formula decomposes into an endpoint term and a derivative correction, while the simplex formula produces endpoint and mixed-derivative terms indexed by the negative coordinates. In the lowest simplex parameter range we use the auxiliary even ultraspherical kernel introduced by Nowak, Sjögren, and Szarek.

candidates.title: On the mode stability of a self-similar blow-up of Yang--Mills heat flow in five dimensions
candidates.comment: 48 pages with appendices, 3 figures, 5 ancillary files
candidates.abstract: We study the spectral stability properties of an explicitly known self-similar blowup profile to the Yang-Mills heat flow on $\mathbb R^5\times SO(5)$ often referred to as the Weinkove solution. We prove that this solution is mode stable in a dynamically evolving DeTurck gauge. To arrive at that result, we first reduce the problem to countably many vector-valued Schrödinger operators on the half line. We then proceed by proving uniform estimates for all but finitely many of said operators. The spectra of the remaining operators are studied individually by means of GGMT bounds or by comparison arguments. Two of these operators are distinguished as they have negative eigenvalues originating from symmetries. Among these two there is a scalar operator, previously analyzed by Donninger and Schörkhuber, and an operator acting on a three-dimensional vector bundle. The latter operator's matrix structure prohibits a straightforward supersymmetric removal. To circumvent this, we transform the equation to a Schrödinger operator with drift terms to simplify the structure of the eigenfunction. candidates.title: The Möbius Homology Laplacian for Persistence Modules
candidates.abstract: Persistent homology provides a framework for studying the evolution of topological features across filtered spaces. While persistence diagrams give discrete invariants that record the birth and death of homological features, they do not directly encode analytic or geometric structure associated to persistence modules. This paper develops a spectral framework for persistent homology by introducing and studying a Laplace operator on the Möbius chain complex, called the Möbius homology Laplacian. Möbius homology categorifies Möbius inversion for persistence modules by replacing integer-valued data with vector-space-valued chain complexes. By equipping these chain complexes with inner products, we define a Laplace operator on the Möbius chain complex whose kernel provides canonical cycle representatives for the associated Möbius homology space. We analyze the spectral properties of this operator in two primary settings: one-parameter persistence modules and birth-death modules arising from filtrations of simplicial complexes. candidates.title: The minimax value of outcome feedback in budget-constrained adaptive sampling
candidates.comment: 16 pages. Ancillary files contain an exact rational certificate and a standard-library Python checker for the computer-assisted part of Section 6
candidates.abstract: Whether adaptivity improves estimation is a classical question in sequential design and information-based complexity. In practice, adaptive data collection can use two different kinds of information: process data on whether each contact succeeded, and the observed outcomes themselves. How much each kind is worth in the worst case under a hard budget has not been settled. We study this question for estimating a common Bernoulli mean through channels with unknown response probabilities and known costs, where failed contacts are charged and the budget must hold on every sample path. We compare static designs, designs that adapt to response indicators only, and fully adaptive designs, each with an arbitrary estimator. Our main theorem shows that when the costs are invariant under a group of channel permutations acting transitively on the nuisance parameter, outcome-adaptive allocation has zero minimax value: response-adaptive and fully adaptive designs have the same minimax risk, given by a one-dimensional optimization and attained by an explicit least-favourable prior and equalizer rule. candidates.title: A fourfold Toda bracket that is not defined, although both threefold subbrackets contain zero
candidates.abstract: We give an explicit example, in the stable homotopy groups of spheres, of a fourfold Toda bracket that is not defined although both of its threefold subbrackets contain zero. Namely, $0\in\langleν^2,2,η^2\rangle$ and $0\in\langle 2,η^2,ν\rangle$, but $\langleν^2,2,η^2,ν\rangle$ has no defining system in the sense of Kochman. This answers a question of Isaksen. The computational input consists only of relations from Toda's book, together with an explicit choice of null-homotopies. The same holds, in the sense of Walker, for the unstable quadruple $(ν_n^2,2ι_{n+6},η_{n+6}^2,ν_{n+8})$ for every $n\ge10$. Moreover, for $n\ge10$, even Cohen's fourfold bracket of this quadruple is empty.

candidates.title: Unknotting number is strictly subadditive for the trefoil
candidates.comment: 8 pages, many figures, Lean verification available, comments welcome
candidates.abstract: A trefoil and a certain fourteen-crossing knot take four crossing changes to unknot separately and at most three together. We extend this example to infinitely many prime partners and show that the same partners give a saving for every nontrivial positive braid knot and, up to mirror, every nontrivial torus knot.

candidates.title: Flag algebras and the exact largest probability of a linear inequality between iid random variables
candidates.abstract: How large can $\mathbb P[X_1+X_2+X_3<2X_4]$ be when $X_1,\dots,X_4$ are independent with a common law $μ$ on $[0,\infty)$? Previous work gave lower bounds through explicit constructions and upper bounds through exchangeability. The best lower bound, $0.4006953723\ldots$, was conjectured by \citet{BF} to be the exact value of the supremum. We prove this conjecture and formalize the proof in Lean~4. The improved upper bound uses the fact that independence gives more than exchangeability: two subsamples are conditionally independent given their shared points. As in Razborov's flag algebras, this yields a semidefinite program on the sign patterns of a few sample points. The new ingredient is to record also whether one sample point exceeds a fixed multiple of another, at ratios read off the extremal construction: with three such cutoffs, four sample points give an exact certificate, while additive comparisons alone leave a gap at seven points. We extend this study to the functions \[ S_2(c) = \sup_μ\mathbb P_μ[X_1+X_2<cX_3],\qquad S_3(c) = \sup_μ\mathbb P_μ[X_1+X_2+X_3<cX_4] \] and determine their exact values on several intervals of $c$. candidates.title: Combined quasi-neutral and zero-relaxation limit of Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we consider the combined quasi-neutral and zero-relaxation limit of Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system. With well-prepared initial, we show that the convergence from Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system for electron and Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system for ion to the incompressible Euler equations and compressible Euler equations, respectively.

candidates.title: A Parallel APSOR SPIKE Algorithm for Classical and Soft Layer Obstacle Problems
candidates.abstract: This paper presents a parallel scheme for classical obstacle problems and for obstacle problems with a soft layer. The adaptive projected SOR method (APSOR) \cite{MS21} finds the contact set on one process. The linear system defined by the frozen contact set is then solved exactly in parallel by the SPIKE algorithm \cite{PS06}, in which the diagonal blocks are factorized independently and the coupling is condensed into a small reduced system. The remaining nonlinearity of the soft-layer problem \cite{CRWX21} is resolved by a Picard iteration in which every pass reuses the factorization, and a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) test stops the iteration. The scheme needs no tuned relaxation parameter. Convergence is proved: APSOR decreases the energy, the SPIKE solve is exact and independent of the number of processes, the Picard iteration is a contraction with factor below $0.052$ on the unit square, and under strict complementarity the loop stops at the unique KKT point. Four classical problems \cite{TSFO14} and four soft-layer examples \cite{CRWX21} in one and two dimensions are computed and compared with exact and analytic solutions (maximum errors $1.1\times10^{-8}$, $7.2\times10^{-14}$

candidates.title: Verified parameter estimation for differential-equation models: NIST reference problems and the theophylline flip-flop
candidates.abstract: Parameters fitted to differential-equation models carry two kinds of error: statistical error from noisy data, and numerical error from the solver and the optimizer that compute the fit. Standard fitting tools report the first and leave the second unexamined, and they return one optimum without saying whether another parameter set fits the data equally well. We describe SIRPY, a differential-equation solver that checks every solution it returns by substituting it back into the equation, and we test it in two settings. First, on eleven nonlinear-regression reference problems from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), each written as a first-order differential equation and fitted by least squares with every model curve supplied by SIRPY, the estimates agree with NIST's certified values to 7.1 to 8.8 significant digits on ten problems, with all 6{,}281 solves verified; the eleventh problem exposed a limitation of the residual check, which we report and explain. candidates.title: Finite conformal models and the Kac--van de Leur conjecture
candidates.abstract: We prove that every simple Lie superalgebra containing the centerless Virasoro algebra, with diagonal $L_0$-action, uniformly bounded weight multiplicities, and support in finitely many cosets of $\Z$, is isomorphic, as a parity-graded Lie superalgebra, to a member of the Witt, special, contact, or Cheng--Kac families. Thus the amended Kac--van de Leur list is exhaustive. Every such algebra admits a finite ordinary conformal model and is a quotient by the full center of a twisted coefficient algebra of a finite simple conformal superalgebra. For Lie superalgebras containing the centerless Virasoro algebra, we also prove that linear commutator growth is equivalent to uniformly bounded weight spaces, provided the grading is diagonal and integral and each weight space is finite-dimensional.

candidates.title: Computer-Aided Analysis of Gradient Descent under Generalized Smoothness
candidates.comment: This is extended version of paper Krivchenko, V. O. (2026). Computer-Aided Analysis of Gradient Descent under Generalized Smoothness. Doklady Mathematics, 530(1), 5-13. The extended version is much more detailed. It contains proper discussion of the approach as well as descriptions of PEP experiments
candidates.abstract: First-order methods constitute a central algorithmic paradigm in high dimensional applications. Under classical assumptions, their performance has been studied quite comprehensively with the developed theoretical apparatus of modern optimization. The development of the Performance Estimation Problems framework led to even deeper understanding and allowed computer-assisted derivation of exact worst-case guarantees. Due to convex nature of PEP programs, the framework is not applicable for systems that involve non-convex constraints. This includes a wide range of non-standard assumptions, some of them are highly relevant for practice such as generalized smoothness. In this paper proposes an approach of utilizing template solutions to derive guarantees in settings that do not admit convex formulation of exact worst-case performance problem. The approach is showcased by studying the performance of the gradient descent method for convex functions that also satisfy generalized smoothness assumption. Despite the inherent conservatism of the approach, this paper improves an existing convergence guarantee in the semi-automated manner.

candidates.title: Efficient numerical computation of the generalized Marcum $Q$-function with applications
candidates.abstract: The computation of the generalized Marcum $Q$-function, $Q_ν(a,b)$, is fundamental to radar detection and wireless communications. The state-of-the-art \textbf{Algorithm 939} (Gil et al., ACM TOMS 2014) serves as the current gold standard by employing a hybrid evaluation scheme combining series expansions, asymptotic formulas, numerical integration and recurrence relations. However, it suffers from a computational bottleneck: in the ``large $a$, small $b$'' regime, the algorithm resorts to computationally expensive numerical quadrature, thereby limiting its overall efficiency. To bridge this gap, we utilize a series representation of the generalized Marcum $Q$-function to construct the Series Expansion based on Recurrence Relations (\textbf{SE-RR}) algorithm. Expanded in powers of $b$, this series computes its coefficients via a stable recurrence relation, resulting in a remarkably low computational cost. By analyzing rounding, truncation and cancellation errors, we identify the optimal region for SE-RR as the ``large $a$, small $b$'' regime, which covers the parameter space where Algorithm~939 relies on costly numerical quadrature. Consequently, we integrate SE-RR into Algorithm~9

candidates.title: Accidental Threefold Dirac Points at the Origin of the Brillouin Zone and Wave-Packet Dynamics
candidates.abstract: We study accidental threefold degeneracies at zero quasimomentum for scalar periodic wave operators on the square lattice. At an isolated positive triple eigenvalue, the middle Bloch band has zero linear term. The two outer bands open linearly in every direction precisely when a Gram matrix of coupling coefficients is positive definite. Square symmetry makes the resulting cone isotropic. For weak perturbations of a constant medium, we construct two transverse tuning curves on which a singlet coincides with a doublet away from their common origin. The central band has positive quadratic curvature along each coordinate axis. For a dilute inclusion of size $η$, a variational gap condition gives a unique transverse crossing in a contrast interval of order $η^{-2}\log(1/η)$. The crossing frequency is asymptotic to $\sqrt{2π/\log(1/η)}$, and the cone speed vanishes linearly with $η$, with a coefficient determined by the far-field dipole moment. A three-component Dirac equation approximates positive-frequency wave packets with an error bound explicit in the material coefficients and the spectral separation at zero quasimomentum. candidates.title: A note on approximate projection onto the semidefinite complementarity set
candidates.abstract: The proximal slack update in an augmented Lagrangian method for semidefinite complementarity constraints requires a joint matrix projection. Given real symmetric matrices $A$ and $B$, we seek the nearest pair $(X,Z)$ with $X$ positive semidefinite, $Z$ negative semidefinite, and $XZ=0$. To approximate this projection, we replace the orthogonal projector onto the subspace allowed for $X$ by a symmetric matrix $T$ with eigenvalues in $[0,1]$. From an optimal solution of the resulting semidefinite program, we form candidate subspaces by starting at the zero subspace and adding the eigenspaces of $T$ in decreasing order of eigenvalue. For each candidate, we compress $A$ to that subspace and $B$ to its orthogonal complement. We keep the positive eigenvalues of the first compression and the negative eigenvalues of the second. The best pair has squared loss at most $1.189$ times the minimum for arbitrary inputs and at most $1.15487$ times the minimum when $A$ is positive semidefinite and $B$ is negative semidefinite. candidates.title: Quaternary games with infinite misère quotients
candidates.abstract: We study the four wild quaternary games left open by the earlier work of Plambeck and Siegel. For \texttt{0.3102} we discover a special regularity of its two--heap case, give a complete solution of the two--heap case, and deduce from it that its misère quotient is infinite. For \texttt{0.3122} and \texttt{0.3123} we rigorously prove, by slice--wise algebraic periodicity and hierarchical induction (computer--assisted), that their misère quotients are infinite. For \texttt{0.3312}, as well as many other wild quaternary games, we carry out computations and observations.

candidates.title: Bruhat Shellings of the Quasisymmetric Flag Moment Complex
candidates.abstract: The quasisymmetric flag variety gives rise to a regular cell complex whose maximal cells are cubes indexed by fully supported noncrossing partitions. Two maximal cubes can meet along several faces. We describe each cube using the block arcs and parent connectors of its indexing partition, and determine its intersection with the union of the preceding cubes in Bruhat order. For each nonempty face, we determine the first maximal cube containing it by applying an outer-block merging operation to its Bruhat-maximal noncrossing-partition label. The first-carrier theorem provides an explicit description of how each cube attaches to the preceding subcomplex. More precisely, the intersection is a union of coordinate facets which, for every cube except the first, forms the closed star of a face in its boundary. Consequently, every linear extension of Bruhat order on the maximal-cell labels gives a shelling of the regular cell complex. In particular, its barycentric subdivision is shellable, hence homotopy Cohen--Macaulay and Cohen--Macaulay over \(\mathbb Z\) and every field.

candidates.title: A Hyper-Reduced Reduced Order Model Built From Streaming Tensor Train Data
candidates.abstract: Low-rank PDE solvers based on tensor-decompositions inside physical space leverages low-rank structures across different physical dimensions, while projection-based reduced order models (ROMs) for parametric PDEs exploit low-rank structures across parameter spaces. Recently, to use the complimentary strength of these two methods, a ROM framework is proposed by incrementally constructing compressed reduced bases directly from streaming tensor-train (TT) snapshots provided by low-rank solvers, but it omits hyper reduction and consequently incur substantial online costs for nonlinear or non-affine parametric PDEs. To address this issue, we develop a hyper-reduced TT ROM for streaming TT data by combining incremental low-rank TT compression and nested TT discrete empirical interpolation (TT-DEIM). Numerical experiments on nonlinear and non-affine parametric PDEs achieve mean relative errors, matching the accuracy of non-hyper-reduced TT-Galerkin ROMs while achieving mean online speedups of approximately 8 times to 1500 times compared to them.

candidates.title: Is every knot a three-way deadlock? Counterexamples and a universality conjecture for the segment number
candidates.comment: 17 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Ancillary files contain the integer coordinates and PD codes of all presentations, the certificates (Reidemeister moves and pass re-routings) and the verification scripts
candidates.abstract: The segment number $s(K)$ of a knot $K$ is the minimal number of arcs into which a diagram of $K$ can be cut so that, for every pair of arcs, one of them passes over the other at all of their common crossings. Every non-trivial knot satisfies $s(K)\ge 3$. In the paper introducing this invariant it was conjectured that the bridge number satisfies $b(K)\le s(K)$, and the torus knot $5_1$ was proposed as a candidate for a knot with $s(K)=4$. We show that both expectations fail: the torus knots $T(2,q)$ with $q=3,5,7,9$ have segment number three, and there is a knot $K$ with $s(K)=3$ and $b(K)\ge 4$, detected by its $3^4$ Fox $3$-colourings. We also give a knot with $s(K)=3$, signature $-6$ and $τ=-3$, so four-dimensional invariants do not bound the segment number from below either; since $g_4(9_1)=4$, even the inequality $g_4(K)\le s(K)$ fails. Both connected sums of two trefoils, the square knot and the granny knot, also have segment number three, although a $3$-segment presentation can never be visibly composite. candidates.title: Product Enrichment of Spline Spaces for IGA: Polynomial Reproduction, Approximation, and Stable Computation
candidates.abstract: We study product enrichment of spline spaces under a fixed isoparametric geometry map for isogeometric analysis (IGA). For each fixed integer $\ell\ge1$, a locally $L^\infty$-stable initial operator reproducing $\mathbb P_k$ yields an explicit linear map from $L^2(D)$ into $W_h^\ell$ that reproduces $\mathbb P_{\ell k}$ and is locally stable in $L^2$ and $L^\infty$, uniformly in the mesh scale. Under additional initial-space regularity and derivative stability, the construction gives integer-order Sobolev error estimates of order $h^{s-m}$ for $1\le s\le\ell k+1$ and admissible $m$. Independently, the geometry representation implies reproduction of physical polynomials of degree at most $\ell$ by the enriched space. Polynomial containment also yields algebraic and analytic best-approximation estimates as the product order increases. For every fixed product order, we give a compatible redundant Galerkin formulation and an explicit initial-space injection. A local spectral construction and an initial-space correction give a two-level energy condition-number bound without requiring independent product generators. candidates.title: Rough structure. I. Exclusion among series-parallel graphs
candidates.abstract: This is the first in a series of papers about rough structure theorems: graph properties that are implied by the exclusion of some graph as a minor, and imply the exclusion of some larger graph of the same type. Here we look at the structure of the series-parallel graphs that do not contain a given series-parallel graph as a minor. We prove that for every series-parallel graph $H$, there exists $m$ such that every simple two-connected series-parallel graph that does not contain $H$ as a minor admits a tree-decomposition of height at most $m$, where each "torso" is either an outerplanar graph or a planar dual of one. We prove similar theorems about the series-parallel graphs that exclude an outerplanar graph, the series-parallel graphs that exclude a dual of an outerplanar graph, the graphs of tree-width three that exclude a series-parallel graph, and the general graphs that exclude a fan.

candidates.title: Counterexamples to the $k$-harmonic conjecture
candidates.abstract: We construct nonminimal $k$-harmonic hypersurfaces in $\R^{n+1}$ for every $k\geq3$ and $n\geq3$, giving counterexamples to the $k$-harmonic conjecture. Each example has exact order $k$ and is an incomplete circular cone or a Euclidean product of such a cone. We also classify the $k$-harmonic circular cones, determine the possible dimensions of nonminimal cones with closed links, and give constructions in higher codimension.

candidates.title: Structure-Preserving Analysis of a Nonlinear Reaction--Diffusion Model for Homogeneous Redox Catalysis
candidates.abstract: We study a reduced nonlinear reaction--diffusion model for homogeneous redox catalysis under a low-scan-rate, frozen-potential approximation motivated by cyclic voltammetry. The reduced system contains two concentration fields coupled through the same nonlinear reaction term and therefore satisfies, exactly within the reduced model, \[ (a-q)_τ=(a-q)_{yy}. \] This identity yields an exact reconstruction of the substrate concentration from the electroactive concentration and provides the organizing principle for the structure-preserving approximations developed below. Formulation I applies the homotopy perturbation method (HPM) to the catalyst field using a constant-coefficient Green-function hierarchy and reconstructs the substrate field from the exact heat equation. Formulation II linearizes the nonlinear reaction about a space- and time-dependent reference profile while preserving the same difference structure and the physical far-field state. The methods are evaluated using fourth-order method-of-lines discretizations, direct Green/heat-kernel formulas for the electrode current, and an independently refined nonlinear PDE benchmark. candidates.title: Sharp Convergence of Extended Douglas--Rachford Splitting with Variable Relaxation
candidates.abstract: We establish a sharp convergence theory for extended Douglas--Rachford splitting when the first operator is maximally monotone and the second is a convex subdifferential on a real Hilbert space. The resolvent stepsizes may be chosen independently, and the relaxation parameter may depend on the current and past iterates. For fixed stepsizes $α,β>0$, let $\vartheta=\min\{2,2α/β\}$. Assuming the sum of the operators has a zero, we prove weak convergence under $0<θ_k\le\vartheta$ and $\sum_kθ_k(\vartheta-θ_k)=\infty$. Within these pointwise bounds, the divergence condition is also necessary for a universal convergence guarantee when the relaxation sequence is prescribed in advance. Constant relaxation recovers the exact range $0<θ<\vartheta$, resolving a conjecture of Nilsson, Åkerman, and Giselsson. We also establish a sharp bound on growth of the residual, defined as the difference between the two resolvent outputs. We combine this bound with a new Lyapunov function whose definition is independent of the relaxation parameter to obtain a last-iterate residual rate, including $o(N^{-1/2})$ when the relaxation parameters remain uniformly separated from both endpoints.

candidates.title: Counting fluctuations in the GOE-GUE crossover
candidates.abstract: We study bulk eigenvalue counting fluctuations in a Gaussian ensemble interpolating between the Gaussian orthogonal and Gaussian unitary ensembles. Realizing this ensemble as the distribution at a fixed time of Hermitian matrix Ornstein-Uhlenbeck flow started from the GOE, we prove a central limit theorem for the one-sided counting function, centered by the semicircle prediction. Its variance grows logarithmically, with a leading coefficient that interpolates between the GOE and GUE values. Specifically, at times $T_N \asymp N^{-1 + \vartheta}$ with fixed $0 < \vartheta < 1$, we prove that the one-sided bulk count is asymptotically Gaussian with leading variance $(1 - \vartheta/2)π^{-2}\log N$. Although the microscopic bulk correlations have their GUE limit throughout this regime, the leading counting variance retains a contribution from the initial GOE matrix.

candidates.title: Feedback Exact Controllability of the Nonlinear Diffusion Equation with Controller in Coefficients
candidates.abstract: One designs a feedback controller for semilinear parabolic equations with controller in diffusion coefficients which steers the initial data y0 in a given state y1 in a finite time.

candidates.title: Killing Scales for Conformal Killing Tensors of Rank Two and Higher
candidates.abstract: We study which metrics in a conformal class admit a Killing tensor with prescribed conformal Killing trace-free part. We call such metrics Killing scales. We also consider whether a given conformal Killing tensor is itself a Killing tensor for some metric in the conformal class, as well as the analogous problem for conformal Killing-Yano forms. Our approach to this problem uses conformal and projective tractors, and the prolongations provided by the BGG splitting operators of the projective and conformal Killing operators. For rank two conformal Killing tensors, we characterise local Killing scales for arbitrary scales on arbitrary conformal manifolds, extending recent results that were restricted to Einstein scales on conformally flat manifolds. The criterion is expressed in terms of the scale tractor and the BGG prolongation of the conformal Killing tensor. We also obtain Killing scale criteria for higher-rank conformal Killing tensors and conformal Killing-Yano forms, under additional hypotheses involving Einstein scales and normal solutions. candidates.title: When do local bounds permit optimal edge-colorings?
candidates.abstract: Let $G$ be a multigraph with maximum degree $Δ(G)$, maximum multiplicity $μ(G)$, and chromatic index $χ'(G)$. A proper edge-coloring is locally bounded if each edge $e$ in $G$ with endvertices $u$ and $v$ is assigned a color at most $\max\{d_G(u)+μ_G(u),d_G(v)+μ_G(v)\}$, where $d_G(w)$ and $μ_G(w)$ respectively denote the degree of $w$ and the maximum multiplicity of an edge incident with $w$. The well-known Vizing's theorem guarantees a proper edge-coloring with at most $Δ(G)+μ(G)$ colors. Recently, the local version of this theorem was established for simple graphs by Christiansen, resolving a conjecture posed by Bonamy, Delcourt, Lang, and Postle, and extended to multigraphs by Conley, Grebík, and Pikhurko. In this paper, we define the local chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $χ'_{loc}(G)$, as the least positive integer $k$ for which $G$ admits a locally bounded proper edge-coloring with colors in $\{1,2,...,k\}$. Thus $Δ(G)\leχ'(G)\leχ'_{loc}(G)\leΔ(G)+μ(G)$. We give equivalent characterizations and sufficient conditions for the equality $χ'_{loc}(G)=χ'(G)$, identifying when the local bounds in Vizing's theorem can be satisfied using the minimum possible number of colors. candidates.title: Random homomorphisms from affine to spherical reflection groups
candidates.abstract: The goal of this paper is to understand the set $\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)$ of homomorphisms from an affine reflection group $\widetilde{W}$ to its associated spherical reflection group $W$. We do this in three ways: numerically, by deriving an explicit formula for $|\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)|$; probabilistically, by exploring the question what does a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}\to W$ look like?; and algebraically, by explicitly writing down all possible homomorphisms on the standard generators. For example, we show that as $n\to\infty$ the probability that a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}_n\to W_n$ is surjective tends to $\frac{3}{4}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n}$ or $D_n$, to $\frac{9}{16}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n+1}$, and to $1$ if $W_n$ is of type $A_n.$

candidates.title: A ring of symmetric Hermitian modular forms of degree $2$ with integral Fourier coefficients II
candidates.abstract: We exhibit 24 homogeneous generators for the graded \(\Z\)-algebra of symmetric Hermitian modular forms of degree 2 over \(\Q(i)\) with integral Fourier coefficients, where the weight \(k\) is even and the character is \(\det^{k/2}\). We prove that 24 is the minimum number of algebra generators. For the subalgebra in weights divisible by 4, Kurihara reduced the generating set given in our earlier work to 11 forms. We show that 13 further forms generate the direct sum of the components in weights congruent to 2 modulo 4 as a module over this subalgebra. For \(p=2\) and \(p=3\), we show that the ring of Fourier expansions modulo \(p\) is a polynomial ring over \(\F_p\) generated by the reductions of 4 forms of weights \(8,12,12,16\). We also record the diagonal Sturm bound \(\lfloor k/8\rfloor\) modulo every prime \(p\) and verify its sharpness in every even weight \(k\ne2\).

candidates.title: The Role of Mathematicians in Mathematics
candidates.abstract: Some reflections on the role of mathematicians in an age of proofs found and verified by machines.

candidates.title: Weighted Carleson embedding on product of trees in general dimension
candidates.abstract: We prove the equivalence of the Carleson embedding on $n$-trees (arbitrary Cartesian product of trees) and the box condition, for arbitrary nonnegative measures and generalized product weights. For product weights, we obtain the sharp coefficient $4^n$. This extends the bi-tree and tri-tree embedding theorems of \cite{AMPVZ} and \cite{MPVZ} to every dimension. We also give two applications of the Carleson embedding: we characterize Carleson measures for the classical Dirichlet space on the polydisc $\mathbb D^n$ and deduce criteria for bounded composition operators from this space into weighted Bergman spaces, generalizing the results from \cite{MPVZ} and \cite{Beslikas2025}. Finally, we define a generalized logarithmic Dirichlet space and characterize its Carleson measures.

candidates.title: Note on the extendability problem for invariant quasimorphisms for mapping class groups
candidates.abstract: In this note, we study the extendability problem of invariant quasimorphisms for short exact sequences related to mapping class groups of surfaces, possibly with one boundary component or one marked point. Using a recent result of Blatz, we prove that if the genus is at least two, then every homogeneous quasimorphism on the Torelli group that is invariant by the conjugation action by the mapping class group is uniquely extendable to the whole mapping class group. Contrastingly, for the surface with one marked point whose genus is at least three, we show the existence of a homogeneous Torelli-group-invariant quasimorphism on the Johnson kernel that is not extendable.

candidates.title: Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli with multilinear weights
candidates.abstract: We study the average distribution of primes up to $x$ in arithmetic progressions to moduli $q$ larger than $\sqrt{x}$, where $q = q_1 \cdots q_n$ ($n \geqslant 2$) with conveniently sized divisors $q_1, \ldots, q_n$ and the average is weighted by an arbitrary divisor-bounded multilinear weight. Specifically, we show that the primes up to $x$ are equidistributed in the residue class $a \pmod{q_1 q_2}$ on average over moduli $q_1 q_2$ as large as $x^{8/15 - \varepsilon}$ when the average is weighted by a bilinear weight and the sizes of $q_1$ and $q_2$ lie in an explicit region, improving the exponent $9/17$ for bilinear weights obtained recently by Li. The new ingredient here is an estimate for the Type-II convolution sums with both factors have size about $x^{1/2}$. With this estimate, the level of distribution $8/15$ in the bilinear case is no longer limited by the Type-II sums but by the Type-I$_3$ sums, or the current range in the ternary divisor problem. We also get further improvements for $n \geqslant 3$ using a simple form of Harman's sieve together with various arithmetic information, including the Type-II estimate mentioned above. candidates.title: Note on OpenAI's proof of the base of Lagrangian fibrations
candidates.abstract: OpenAI proved that every Lagrangian fibration of a compact hyper-Kähler manifold has a base $\mathbb P^n$. This expository note summarizes the last section of their paper.

candidates.title: A bound for Stieltjes constants of the Riemann zeta function
candidates.abstract: The coefficients appearing in the Laurent expansion of the Riemann zeta function are known as the Stieltjes constants and are denoted by $γ_n$. Several authors, including Berndt, Matsuoka, Williams and Zhang, and Saad Eddin, have investigated upper bounds for $|γ_n|$, with the best known result due to Pauli and Saidak \cite{MR4671618}. In 2003, based on numerical evidence, Kreminski \cite{MR1972742} conjectured that Matsuoka's bound \cite{MR827790} could be considerably improved. Motivated by this conjecture, we employ the saddle-point method to derive an asymptotic formula for the Stieltjes constants, with the saddle point expressed explicitly in terms of the Lambert $W$-function. The resulting formula yields an asymptotic upper bound of the correct order of magnitude. Moreover, the resulting bound is consistent with the conjecture of Farr, Pauli, and Saidak \cite{MR4280128}.

candidates.title: On the performance of the randomized Euler scheme for nonlinear ODEs under inexact information
candidates.abstract: We analyze the randomized explicit Euler scheme for nonlinear ordinary differential equations under a local one-sided Lipschitz condition, local Hölder regularity in the space variable, and Hölder regularity in the time variable. We allow for noisy evaluations of the right-hand side. For the resulting approximation, we derive an error bound in which the contribution associated with the Hölder regularity in the time variable exhibits the characteristic 1/2-order gain of randomized methods. While existing results cover deterministic schemes under the one-sided Lipschitz condition and randomized schemes under the classical Lipschitz condition, our results combine randomized approximation and one-sided Lipschitz regularity.

candidates.title: Linear and non-linear integro-differential equations with variable coefficients and Sonin kernels
candidates.comment: Accepted for publication in Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
candidates.abstract: We study linear and non-linear integro-differential equations, with Sonin and absolutely continuous kernels, and with variable coefficients which are either integrable or continuous functions. In the linear case, for all cases, the unique solution is given explicitly by a convergent infinite series involving compositions of convolutions of the kernels and the variable coefficients. Many examples are provided. For the non-linear case, the existence and uniqueness are established under a suitable condition in the non-linear term. The analytic solution is given by the limit of the iterative sequence found from the method of successive approximations. The exact analytical expressions for several problems are found by computing the iterative sequences that approximate the solution.

candidates.title: An Exact Penalty Method for Large-Scale Equality-Constrained Nonlinear Optimization
candidates.abstract: We present an exact penalty method for equality-constrained nonlinear optimization. Our approach transforms the smooth, constrained problem into a sequence of nonsmooth, unconstrained problems by penalizing the constraint violation by its Euclidean norm. An outer loop updates the penalty parameter and the subproblem tolerances, while an inner loop solves each penalized subproblem with a quadratic regularization method. The method also includes a local infeasibility detection mechanism, an extrapolation strategy for warm-starting subproblems, and nonmonotone acceptance rules. We establish global convergence to first-order stationary points under a bounded penalty parameter assumption, with a worst-case complexity of \(\mathcal{O}(|\log ε|\,ε^{-2})\) inner iterations. We implement the method in Penelopt, an open-source Julia solver for constrained nonlinear optimization. On \(224\) problems from the CUTEst collection, Penelopt is competitive with IPOPT and more robust than the recent solvers MadNLP and Uno. candidates.title: Automorphism groups of Severi--Brauer varieties of odd prime degree over $\mathbb{Q}$
candidates.abstract: We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroup of automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer variety of odd prime degree $p$ over the field of rational numbers is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}.$

candidates.title: Parallel batch scheduling for optimizing hospital sterilization operations: arc-flow formulations, column generation and Lagrangian heuristics for flowtime minimization
candidates.comment: Submitted to European Journal of Operational Research
candidates.abstract: In a recent work by Schlembach et al., the problem of optimally managing sterilization operations in hospitals has been modeled as a machine scheduling problem with parallel batch processing and minimum flowtime objective, and heuristically solved by column generation. We draw upon this approach, developing arc-flow formulations and related column-generation procedures, using an exact dynamic programming algorithm to solve the pricing problems. We further derive Lagrangian relaxations based on minimum cost flows and shortest paths, with subgradient optimization and the volume algorithm guiding batch generation. A makespan bound for schedules minimizing total flow time provides a finite horizon when no operational limit is known. Computational experiments on literature benchmarks and more challenging generated instances demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches. The arc-flow model solves all literature benchmark instances to proven optimality within seconds, while the Lagrangian heuristics deliver high-quality schedules with substantially reduced computational effort.

candidates.title: The Dunford-Pettis property and complemented Hilbert subspaces of Sobolev martingale spaces
candidates.abstract: Let $L^1_W$ be the space of integrable terminal values of martingales on a homogeneous tree whose local differences belong to a fixed matrix space $W$. We show that $L^1_W$ has the Dunford-Pettis property if and only if $W$ is spanned by its rank-one matrices. Every complemented reflexive subspace of $L^1_W$ is isomorphic to a Hilbert space. Under the second structural condition of Ayoush, Stolyarov and Wojciechowski, the martingale fractional integral of order $\frac12$ is completely continuous and fails to be absolutely $2$-summing. This gives nonisomorphism with $L^1$ for $W\ne0$. On the $4$-ary tree we exhibit all three possible combinations of the Dunford-Pettis property and the existence of a complemented copy of $\ell^2$. In one example a bounded operator into $\ell^4$ fails to be completely continuous, although every bounded operator into a Hilbert space is completely continuous. We also prove that, for every $n\ge1$, each complemented reflexive subspace of $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^n)$ is isomorphic to a Hilbert space.

candidates.title: The coordinate dependence of numerical rank: charts adapted to level sets
candidates.abstract: Sampling a smooth field on a grid can give an array of high numerical rank even when the field is simple. A Gaussian ridge rotated off the grid axes is the standard example: in coordinates which follow the ridge, the same field has rank one. The rank therefore depends on the chart, that is, on the coordinates in which the field is sampled. We ask which properties of a chart control this rank. First, mesh quality does not control rank: a chart whose cells have perfect size and shape can still give infinite rank. Second, when a chart follows the level sets of an estimate of $φ$, the extra rank depends on a single quantity, the defect, which measures how much the true field varies along each coordinate line. candidates.title: A Principled Framework for PDE-Based Shock Capturing in High-Order Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
candidates.comment: 34 pages, 27 figures, 10 tables. Submitted to the Journal of Computational Physics
candidates.abstract: PDE-based artificial viscosity (AV) captures shocks in high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods by solving an auxiliary PDE for a smooth viscosity field. The behavior of that field is set by how the terms of the AV PDE scale with the element size $h$ and polynomial degree $p$, and by how its coefficients are parametrized. This work derives both choices from analysis and studies the impact these choices have on the implicit steady-state solver. First, an $L^2$-projection analysis shows that the thinnest shock a polynomial space can represent monotonically scales with the resolution length $\bar h = h/p$, and a scaling analysis of the AV PDE gives concrete conditions on its diffusion and source terms for the solution to be self-similar in $\bar h$. Prior formulations satisfy them only under $h$-refinement at fixed $p$; the AV PDE is scaled so that they hold under $hp$-refinement, and the captured shock thins accordingly. Second, a Green's-function analysis of the steady AV PDE gives closed-form expressions for the width and magnitude of the AV. candidates.title: On derived Galois deformation rings in characteristic 0 and a conjecture of Venkatesh
candidates.abstract: Let $Π$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\operatorname{GL}_n$ over a CM field $F$, and $ρ$ its associated Galois representation in characteristic 0. With mild assumptions, we use the Taylor--Wiles method to define a free action of the potentially semistable derived deformation ring of $ρ$ on the $Π$-part of the $p$-adic cohomology of $\operatorname{GL}_n/F$, confirming a prediction of Venkatesh. As a key step, we establish an equivalence between the derived deformation ring of $ρ$ with the completion at the point corresponding to $ρ$ of the derived deformation ring of the mod $p$ reduction $\barρ$, generalising well-known results by Kisin.

candidates.title: Improved Omega results for Riesz sums of a class of $L$-functions
candidates.abstract: We investigate a general class of $L$-functions satisfying functional equations with multiple gamma factors, and establish sharper lower bounds for the error terms associated with the Riesz sums of their coefficients. By integrating the resonance method with Riesz smoothing, we improve upon previously known omega results for the corresponding Riesz sums. We prove these estimates within a unified axiomatic framework under a precise set of hypotheses. Our general theorem can be applied to several classical arithmetic problems, including the $k$-fold Piltz divisor function $d_{\mathbb{K},k}(n)$ over a number field $\mathbb{K}$, as well as the lattice point counting functions for the circle, ellipse, and sphere problems. In particular, we sharpen the classical $Ω$-bound for the error in counting lattice points in the ellipse $u^2+5v^2\le x$, strengthening a result of Nowak. Moreover, for the smoothed error terms corresponding to the divisor and circle problems, we improve upon previously known $Ω$-bounds by increasing the exponent of the $\log\log x$ factor and sharpening the $\log\log\log x$ dependence by replacing exponential decay factors of the form $\exp(-c\sqrt{\log\log\log x})$
